dedupe_keys.name: daily large hail probability on a global scale 1979 to 2015 version 2

description: This dataset by Andreas Prein and Greg Holland, archived at PANGAEA as a supplement to their 2018 paper Global estimates of damaging hail hazard in Weather and Climate Extremes, gives daily gridded estimates of the probability of large hail (diameter above 2.5 cm) worldwide from 1979 to 2015. The estimates come from the presence of environmental conditions in which large hail has been observed, applied to reanalysis fields, on a global grid of 0.7 by 0.7 degrees; values run from zero to one, where one means a high probability that the location sees large hail on that day. The PANGAEA record is version 2 and lists links to the NetCDF files (222 file entries in a tab-separated table); it is free under the Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 licence, as the DataCite metadata read on 2026-09-28 state. Caveats: it is a statistical proxy of hail-favourable conditions, not observed hail reports, the grid is coarse for local assets, and the series ends in 2015 with no update since 2018. It serves hazard exposure and resilience analysis of assets sensitive to hail, such as solar farms, overhead lines, vehicles and building roofs. No other catalogued record gives global hail climatology; the hail value was added to the hazard vocabulary on 2026-09-26 for resources like this one.
